Text goes in single quotes; numbers and NULL do not', which points at quoting, not at the common result type. [round 1, 8a7daa17] Verified. Every unreadable statement, the empty-file prompt and every real subset limit reach the shell as kind 'limit' from the adapter's check() in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/engine.js; I reproduced 'SELEC * FROM students;', a missing comma between two VALUES rows, a missing semicolon before a second SELECT and the untouched starter, all kind 'limit'. authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js relabels 'limit' as 'Not in this practice editor', and LIMITS item 4 in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/build.mjs plus every page's Sources footer ('not as invalid PostgreSQL') say that label never means the SQL is wrong. The label is page-owned, so it is fixable in scope. Acceptable fix: in controller.js, wrap EDITOR.check (EDITOR is Object.create of the adapter) and re-kind problems by message into three classes. Real subset limits (WITH, psql meta-commands, CREATE TABLE and so on) keep 'Not in this practice editor'. Unreadable statements ('could not read the statement near', 'could not read one starting') get a learner label such as 'Check your SQL'. The empty-file prompt gets its own neutral label. Message matching is feasible: I checked that real limits carry their own messages ('WITH queries are outside this practice editor', 'CREATE is not available here', 'Transactions are outside this practice editor', 'COPY runs on the database server', and the psql meta-command text), distinct from the unreadable-statement messages. Never use the adapter's own 'Lesson check' (B4), and never use kind 'hint', because the shell blocks Run only on non-hint problems. Run gating, the 'limit' notRun status and onSqlRun's 'did not use up a try' path must stay exactly as they are (E2 is pending). Reword LIMITS item 4 and the footer sentence in each src/<topic>.body.html and artifact.md to match. The minimum acceptable fix, if message matching seems too brittle, is one neutral label covering both cases, with LIMITS and footer sentences that no longer say the SQL is fine. Shell wording stays a recipe finding.

The authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/build.mjs badge reads 'Practice editor: follows PostgreSQL on this page's sample tables' and the status span reads 'SQL practice editor'. CONF in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/build.mjs prints Low / Medium / High, but DESIGN.md (Assessment: options, confidence, feedback) sets "Guessing", "Fairly sure", "Certain". In authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js, checkPredict writes 'Your guess was not this time', and summarize() joins open activities as 'Activity '+open.join(' and '), which gives 'Activity 2 and 3 and 4 are'. [round 1, 8a7daa17] Reproduced at 570x1000 under file:// and over http://127.0.0.1: scrollY 157, exactly the top of #activity-1. At 1280 px it is 121 on inner-and-left-joins and 0 where the document fits. Cause confirmed: with history.replaceState stubbed out, scrollY stays 0. The last line of authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js calls go(...,'replace'), whose history.replaceState(#activity-1) runs during parsing. It does not throw, and the browser's load-time scroll-to-fragment then scrolls to #activity-1, so F1 fails on the narrow frame (G7). Fix in controller.js: on first load with no #activity-N in the URL, do not write a hash (call go with no history mode), or write it after load and keep scroll at 0. Keep the hash behaviour for later navigation. Measured in headless Chromium only; check the platform embed after the fix.
